title: Evaluating Teams End to End
objective: After this lesson you will be able to build team gold runs with per-agent attribution, distinguish handoff vs node vs delegation failures, diff versions per segment, and gate shipping on team-level no-regressions.
why: Unit-tested agents fail as teams: dropped handoffs, misdelegations, and shared-state misreads exist only in composition. Team gold runs (conversations with expected terminals + per-agent expectations + forbiddens) attribute end-to-end outcomes to components — the only evaluation that catches integration truth. Ship on team deltas, not agent averages.

blocks.text: Team gold items assert per-agent expectations: triage routed shipping (router), decider approved with reason (node), draft ≤60 words (contract), no direct refund (forbidden). Each expectation names its owner — failures arrive pre-attributed. Cover happy/edge/attack conversations; every production team incident becomes a gold item with the failing agent named.

blocks.caption: Expectations owned per agent; forbiddens guard team-level invariants

blocks.text: Team failures sort into three bins. **Node**: right terminal, wrong content (bad draft — fix the agent). **Handoff**: right agents, broken transfer (missing confidence — fix the contract/gate). **Delegation**: wrong agent did the work (shipping handled by billing — fix router/manager). Attribution decides the fix location; misattribution (retraining the drafter for a router error) wastes cycles.

blocks.caption: Slot-by-slot attribution: failures arrive with owner names attached

blocks.text: Version diffs per segment, gate on teams

Same-set, per-kind diffs (happy/edge/attack) with segment gates — the LangGraph Ch.9 discipline unchanged, now attributing per agent. v2's VIP regression blocks shipping regardless of averages; the fix's owner comes from attribution (router? node? handoff?). Team eval reuses every single-graph practice; only the attribution slots are new.

blocks.title: Attribute the failure
blocks.note: Run it: expect pass with [] then fail naming triage.category — attribution to the agent, not the team. Fix location decided by the issue string, before any code changes.

items: Gold runs assert per-agent slots + team forbiddens across happy/edge/attack
Attribution bins: node (content) vs handoff (transfer) vs delegation (routing) — fix location follows
Same-set per-segment diffs gate shipping; incidents become named gold items

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice checker on both runs and map verdicts. (b) Extend the gold with a forbid (direct-refund) and a failing run triggering it; confirm the issue names the invariant. (c) Attribute: terminal correct, draft over length, confidence missing — three faults, three bins, three owners.
hints: Good passes []; bad fails [triage.category] — owner named, fix located upstream of draft.
Forbid check scans the serialized result: inject 'direct-refund' into a bad run's actions and watch forbidden fire.
Terminal correct + overlong draft → node (drafter contract); missing confidence → handoff (triage gate); wrong agent acted → delegation (router).
exercise.why: Attribution precision across three bins is the team-debugging skill: same symptom class, three different owners, three different fixes. Misattribution wastes the most expensive cycles in team maintenance.
exercise.code: // Attribution drill: per fault, bin + owner + fix location stated.

quiz.q: All agent unit tests pass; customers get wrong refunds. Missing?
options: Team gold runs with per-agent attribution: composition failures (handoffs, delegation) exist only end to end
quiz.explain: Integration truth lives in composition: transfers, routing choices, shared reads. Gold runs with attribution catch what unit tests structurally cannot.

quiz.q: Correct terminal, overlong draft. Fault bin + owner?
quiz.explain: Content faults belong to producing nodes and their contracts. Terminal correctness exonerates routing; length terms indict the drafter.

quiz.q: v2 wins overall, regresses VIP. Ship?
options: No — per-segment no-regression gate; fix VIP path first (team eval inherits single-graph discipline)
quiz.explain: Segment gates transfer unchanged to teams. Averages hide localized harm; VIP regressions block shipping.

summary: Per-agent gold slots, three-bin attribution (node/handoff/delegation), same-set segment diffs, ship on team deltas. Composition tested as composition.
next: Proven patterns need their pathology counterpart: drift, loops, bloat, conflicts — and the fixes that hold. Next: team failure modes.
